answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive: every new agent must forge a bonded deposit before it may act, and peers who detect duplicated content can slash that bond. Each message gets a unique content hash, attested by a rotating group of independent peers. If two accounts publish the same text, both bonds burn, so running many clones costs more than it earns. A public mesa of staked registries tracks who vouched for whom, and a terrace of auditors publishes every slash on-ledger. Attackers can spin up accounts, but not cheap ones.
